files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.AppConfig

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.CommandHandler
files.Summary: Handles console command input and execution for the daemon. Provides commands for starting, stopping, restarting, querying status, and shutting down monitored applications.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.ConsoleCommand
files.Summary: Represents a console command that can be executed by the daemon. Encapsulates command name, description, and execution logic. Validates all parameters at construction time to fail fast on misconfiguration.

files.Summary: Connects this daemon to the database-backed control plane: reports what it supervises, and executes the commands an operator queued for this host.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.DaemonOrchestrator
files.Summary: Orchestrates the lifecycle of application health monitors. Owns daemon-wide state (cancellation, start signal, active monitors) and pre-validates configurations at construction time.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.HealthCheckerFactory
files.Summary: Creates instances for the specified port types. Returns an empty list when no port types are configured (process-only monitoring). Logs a warning when UDP is the only configured port type, as it provides no real health signal.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.HealthMonitor
files.Summary: Monitors the health and lifecycle of a single application process. Provides automatic restart capabilities, resource monitoring, and port health checks.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.HealthMonitorStatus
files.Summary: Immutable snapshot of a 's current state for diagnostics.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.IHealthChecker
files.Summary: Defines a contract for checking the health of a specific port type. Implementations should handle their own timeout and cleanup logic.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.ISupervisionHost
files.Summary: The seam through which a whose monitoring loop has ended asks to be supervised again, without knowing anything about how the monitoring cycle is run.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.ISupervisionReservation
files.Summary: A held place in a running monitoring cycle. See .

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.PortType
files.Summary: The health checks an application can be configured with.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.PulseHealthChecker
files.Summary: Checks a FishMMO game server by reading the pulse it writes to the database.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.TcpHealthChecker
files.Summary: Checks port health by attempting to establish a TCP connection. Uses a linked cancellation token to enforce timeouts without leaking timers.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.TerminalProcessLauncher
files.Summary: Launches through a terminal without confusing its PID with the supervised app.

files.Title: AppHealthMonitor.UdpHealthChecker
files.Summary:
Checks port health by attempting to send a UDP datagram.

Limitation: UDP is connectionless. A successful send only confirms the local OS accepted the datagram into the send buffer, not that the remote endpoint received it or is alive. This checker will report success even if the target application is down. For reliable health checking, prefer TCP, or DatabasePulse for a FishMMO game server. Use UDP only as a supplementary probe alongside other port types.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.AccessLevel
files.Summary:
Account and character access levels. Values must stay in sync with FishMMO.Database.Data.Enums.AccessLevel.

WARNING: If you add, remove, or reorder a value here you MUST update the corresponding enum in the database layer and run a migration. Consider adding a unit test that asserts every member of this enum matches the database enum (e.g. via a SELECT DISTINCT query or a checked-in mapping file) so the mismatch is caught at CI time rather than at runtime.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.AccountVerifyDto

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.ClientAuthResultDto

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.Collections.ArrivalOrderTracker<TKey>

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.Collections.ExpiringKeyTracker<TKey>

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.Collections.FixedWindowCounter<TKey>

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.Collections.PendingAuthTracker<TConnection>
files.Summary: Connections that have completed their handshake and not yet authenticated, each in a , with expiry swept head-first in the order they fall due.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Core.CreateAccountDto

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.AccountData
files.Summary: Holds account-related data for a server session, including authentication state, access level, and optional SRP authentication data.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.AccountManager<TConnection>
files.Summary: Thread-safe base manager for account and connection data, including encryption state and the unified machine. All public methods are synchronized via a shared lock to support concurrent access from network broadcast handlers and async worker threads. Subclass or for authentication-method-specific behaviour.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.BaseAuthenticatorCore<TConnection>
files.Summary:
Abstract engine-independent base for all server authenticators. Provides X25519 ECDH handshake logic, stale-auth TTL sweeps, per-IP and global handshake rate limiting, and connection auth-state tracking — with no dependency on Unity, FishNet, or any game-engine type.

Concrete implementations supply transport-specific callbacks (broadcast, disconnect, IP resolution) by implementing the abstract members, then call from their transport layer.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.ClientAuthenticatorCore
files.Summary:
Engine-independent client-side authenticator state machine. Implements the full SRP-6a + X25519 ECDH client auth flow, including cookie challenge echo, key agreement, token auth (World/Scene), SRP verify/proof, TOTP, and key material cleanup.

Concrete implementations (e.g., FishNet ClientLoginAuthenticator) implement abstract callbacks for broadcasting messages and notifying the application layer.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.ClientSrpData
files.Summary: Holds SRP (Secure Remote Password) authentication data and logic for a client-side session.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.ConnectionEncryptionData
files.Summary:
Holds per-connection encryption state including directional AES keys, nonce contexts, and negotiated protocol version. Keys are established via X25519 ECDH key agreement during the handshake phase.

Thread-safety: nonce contexts use Interlocked internally for counter operations.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper.AuthMessageType
files.Summary: Message type identifiers for AAD binding. Values are fixed and must be used by both client and server.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper.NonceSide
files.Summary: Disposable container that owns a GCM session prefix and provides thread-safe nonce generation. Zeroes the prefix on dispose to prevent accidental reuse across sessions.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper.SessionKeys
files.Summary: Container for derived session keys and prefixes.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper.TwoFactor
files.Summary: TOTP two-factor authentication helpers. Uses OtpNet for TOTP generation/verification, AES-256-GCM for encrypting TOTP secrets at rest, and PBKDF2-SHA256 for hashing recovery codes.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper.X25519EphemeralKeyPair
files.Summary: Disposable container for an ephemeral X25519 keypair that enforces private-key zeroization via API ownership. The private key is never exposed to callers.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.CryptoHelper
files.Summary: Static class providing cryptographic helper methods for X25519 ECDH key agreement, AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption, HKDF-SHA256 key derivation, HMAC-SHA256 signing, and authentication token management. BouncyCastle is used for cross-platform support on all Unity targets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.HandshakeService.ServerKeyAgreementResult

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.HandshakeService

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.IKmsProvider

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.KeyEnvelope

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.ProcessHardening

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.SrpAuthenticatorCore<TConnection>
files.Summary:
Engine-independent SRP-6a authenticator core for LoginServer use. Extends with bounded-channel SRP verify/proof workers, TOTP two-factor authentication, kick-request tracking, and per-IP/per-account rate limiting — with no dependency on Unity, FishNet, or any game-engine type.

Subclasses provide transport-specific callbacks for broadcasting auth results, disconnecting connections, resolving IP addresses, and performing database operations.

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.TokenAccountManager<TConnection>

files.Title: FishMMO.Auth.Implementation.TokenAuthenticatorCore<TConnection>

Engine-independent token-based authenticator core for World/Scene servers. Extends with a bounded-channel token auth worker that decrypts, verifies, and revocation-checks client-supplied auth tokens issued by the LoginServer.

Subclasses supply transport-specific callbacks (broadcast, database validation).

files.Summary: Represents the result of a database operation with success/failure status and optional data. Type-safe alternative to tuples that provides consistent error handling across all database operations. Follows Functional Programming principles: explicit success/failure handling without exceptions for expected failures.

files.Title: FishMMO.Database.DatabaseSecrets
files.Summary:
Secure resolver for database connection parameters.

Resolution order (first wins):

  1. Environment variables (FISHMMO_DB_*)
  2. Platform secrets file:
    • Linux: /etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env
    • Windows: %ProgramData%\FishMMO\db-secrets.env

The secrets file is a simple KEY=VALUE format (one per line,

comments and blank lines ignored). On Linux it should be

chmod 600 owned by the service user.

appsettings.json MUST NOT contain Username or Password fields. Those fields have been removed from the configuration model entirely — there is no IConfiguration fallback for credentials.

files.Title: FishMMO.Database.Exceptions.DatabaseException
files.Summary: Base exception for all database-related errors in the FishMMO database layer. Provides safe error messages for client communication while preserving detailed information for logging. Follows Open/Closed Principle: extensible through inheritance for specific error types.

files.Title: FishMMO.Database.Exceptions.DuplicateReplayException
files.Summary: Thrown when a version-gated write is attempted with an incoming Version equal to the persisted Version. This represents a duplicate replay (or double-submit) and must not be treated as success.

files.Title: FishMMO.Database.Exceptions.StaleStateException
files.Summary: Thrown when an operation fails due to stale state (optimistic concurrency violation). The incoming version is behind the persisted version, indicating a conflicting write occurred. This is a non-transient, non-retryable logical failure.

files.Title: FishMMO.Installer.AppSettingsInstaller
files.Summary:
Interactive wizard that creates or updates appsettings.json and related configuration files with secure file permissions (chmod 600 on Linux). Also generates environment-variable export files so passwords never need to live in plain-text JSON at rest.

Supported components:

  • IPFetch Web Server — WebServer.HttpPort + ConnectionStrings.NpgsqlConnection
  • Patcher Web Server — WebServer.HttpPort + Patches.DirectoryName
  • WebGL Web Server — WebServer.HttpPort
  • Control Panel Web Server — WebServer.HttpPort + ConnectionStrings.NpgsqlConnection
  • Discord Bot — Discord.DefaultGuildId + Npgsql (host, port, database, schema) + chat bridge + rate-limiting. Its token and database credentials are secrets and live only in the shared secrets file ().

Supported outputs:

  • appsettings.json — base configuration, chmod 600
  • appsettings.Development.json / appsettings.Production.json — environment overrides, chmod 600
  • fish shell snippet — ~/.config/fish/conf.d/fishmmo-secrets.fish, chmod 600
  • systemd / .env file — fishmmo-secrets.env in target directory, chmod 600

Database credentials (Username/Password) are NOT stored in appsettings.json. They are resolved at runtime via the DatabaseSecrets class from environment variables (FISHMMO_DB_USERNAME, FISHMMO_DB_PASSWORD) or the platform secrets file (/etc/fishmmo/db-secrets.env on Linux).

files.Title: FishMMO.Installer.SecurityKeyInstaller
files.Summary:
Generates cryptographic keys for FishMMO deployments and stores them directly in the database using a superuser connection. No env files to copy between machines — every server loads its keys from the DB at startup.

Keys managed:

  • Gate secret → deployment_secrets table (key='client_gate_secret')
  • Connection token HMAC key → connection_token_keys table (key_id='shared')
  • Signing key KEK → deployment_secrets table (key='signing_key_kek')
  • TOTP master KEK → deployment_secrets table (key='totp_master_kek')

Client build files (ClientApiSecret.generated.cs, etc.) are generated separately from within the Unity Editor (FishMMO > Security > Fetch Client Secrets).

Uses a superuser NpgsqlConnection — matching the pattern established by InstallFishMMODatabase and GrantUserPermissions. The caller is responsible for obtaining the superuser credentials (via HandleWithSuperuser or the FISHMMO_PG_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD environment variable).

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.ClientCertificatePinning
files.Summary:
Centralised TLS certificate pinning for outbound UnityWebRequest traffic (launcher version probe, patch download, login-server discovery, renewal endpoints, etc.).

Pins are SHA-256 hashes of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) DER encoding, base64-encoded — the same format used by HPKP / RFC 7469. SPKI pinning is preferred over full-certificate pinning because it survives certificate renewals as long as the underlying key pair is reused, and is preferred over CA pinning because it cannot be bypassed by any CA in the trust store.

Unity's CertificateHandler.ValidateCertificate(byte[]) only exposes the leaf certificate, so this implementation deliberately ignores chain validity and instead requires that the leaf's SPKI match a known-good pin. Always configure at least two pins (active + backup) so an emergency key rotation does not require a client patch.

IL2CPP / AOT platforms (WebGL, iOS, consoles): BouncyCastle relies on runtime reflection for algorithm lookup and type activation. Without linker instructions, the managed-code linker will strip the types it needs. Ensure Assets/link.xml includes: <assembly fullname="Org.BouncyCastle" preserve="all"/>.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.ClientGateSecret
files.Summary:
IL-embedded client gate secret.

The default here is a sentinel, and this file is tracked so the project always compiles. The real value lives in the gitignored ClientApiSecret.generated.cs, written by FishMMO Dashboard > Game Settings (or by CI substituting FISHMMO_CLIENT_GATE_SECRET into GeneratedFileTemplates/ClientApiSecret.generated.cs.template), which implements to overwrite it. See for why the generated file no longer declares the whole class.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.ClientSecurityBootstrap
files.Summary:
Initialises before any scene loads or UnityWebRequest is dispatched. Pin sources, in order:

  1. CertificatePins.generated.cs — IL-embedded pins written by FishMMO > Security > Fetch Certificate Pins. The committed source contains sentinel placeholders; the editor tool overwrites them.

  2. API pin update manifest (optional, async) — fetched from GET {APIHost}config/pins, verified against an Ed25519 public key embedded alongside the pins. Only ADDS pins; never removes. Failures are silent — the compile-time pin set remains active.

There is NO StreamingAssets fallback. Pins are always IL-embedded.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.Ed25519ManifestVerifier

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.IPinUpdateSidecar
files.Summary:
Scaffold interface for out-of-band TLS pin updates.

This is a forward-planning scaffold only. No production implementation is currently wired into the client. The default is always returned, meaning the static pin set from is never overridden at runtime.

Hard-coded compile-time pins (see ) require shipping a new client build to rotate keys. That is unacceptable when a CA-incident or HSM rotation forces an emergency pin swap on a faster cadence than the client release pipeline.

The intended production implementation:

  • Fetches a signed manifest (Ed25519 / RSA-PSS) from a well-known URL,
  • Verifies the signature against a compile-time embedded public key (a separate trust anchor from the TLS PKI it is updating!),
  • Returns the new pin set with an effective-from / expires-at window so the bootstrap can reject stale manifests.

The bootstrap MUST treat sidecar failures as advisory only and never downgrade pinning below what was statically configured. A compromised sidecar host must not be able to remove pins — only narrow them.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.NullPinUpdateSidecar

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.PinUpdateManifest

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.TwoFactorRecoveryCrypto
files.Summary:
Password-based authenticated encryption for the local 2FA recovery-code payload.

Why the account password and not a machine-bound key. The obvious alternative is a key sealed to the machine (DPAPI, keychain, a file next to the payload). That protects the codes from another local process, but it dies with the installation — and a reinstall, a new machine or a wiped profile is precisely the situation in which a player reaches for recovery codes. A machine-bound key would therefore trade a confidentiality problem for an availability one, and locking a player out of their own account is the worse failure of the two. The account password is in hand at exactly the two moments that matter — when the codes are written at 2FA setup, and when the player legitimately asks to read them back — and it is the one secret that survives a reinstall.

Primitives. Argon2id and AES-256-GCM, both from the BouncyCastle build this project already ships (Assets/Dependencies/BouncyCastle.Cryptography.dll) and already depends on for all of its other crypto. No new dependency. BouncyCastle rather than System.Security.Cryptography.AesGcm for the same reason CryptoHelper.EncryptAES uses it: it behaves identically on every Unity player target, where the BCL AEAD types are not uniformly available.

Why Argon2id rather than the PBKDF2 the server uses for recovery-code hashing. CryptoHelper.TwoFactor.HashRecoveryCode is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600k iterations because it runs server-side, once per verification, against a high-entropy random code. This runs client-side, twice per account lifetime, against a human-chosen password, and the attacker is someone who already has the file. Memory-hardness is the property that matters there, and the parameters are recorded in the envelope so they can be raised later without stranding files written by an older client.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.TwoFactorRecoveryReadResult

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.Security.TwoFactorRecoveryStore
files.Summary:
The local, on-disk copy of the 2FA setup payload (otpauth URI + recovery codes) written during account creation so the player still has the codes if the client dies before they finish writing them down.

The payload used to be a plaintext .txt. Randomising the filename and tightening the permissions — the previous pass — removed the account-name leak and the guessable path, but the contents were still readable by anything that could open the file: another local user on a machine where the chmod did not take, a backup agent, a sync client, a stolen disk. This class encrypts the payload under the account password; see for why the password and not a machine-bound key.

Every method here is deliberately non-destructive on failure. The one thing this storage must never do is destroy a payload the player has not yet copied down.

files.Title: FishMMO.Client.UITKDeathDialog
files.Summary:
Death dialog shown when the local player dies. Offers two options: "Respawn at Bind Point" (always visible) and "Accept Resurrect" (appears when another player casts resurrect on the corpse). Sends the appropriate broadcast on button click and hides on success.

There is deliberately no close button. Respawning or being resurrected are the only ways out of the dead state, and both are reached through this dialog — a control that merely dismissed it would leave the player a corpse with no route back, because the server only re-sends DeathBroadcast on scene entry.

Two properties keep a character from getting stuck dead:

  • It opens from state, not just from a message. A character that arrives already dead — a login while dead, or a scene transfer while dead — surfaces the dialog from , which reads the replicated flag out of the spawn payload. That does not depend on a DeathBroadcast arriving at the right moment relative to the world GUI scene finishing its load.
  • It confirms rather than assumes. Clicking an action used to hide the dialog immediately, so a request the server declined — its respawn/resurrect ingress guard debounces at two seconds — left the player dead with no UI and no way to ask again. The dialog now stays up until the character is actually observed alive, and re-arms itself if that never happens.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Core.Collections.InstanceCapacityHeap
files.Summary:
A max-heap of scene instances, keyed by scene row ID, ordered by remaining capacity. Used for O(log N) fallback instance selection in open-world routing.

The root always holds the instance with the most remaining capacity. peeks the root, decrements its capacity, and re-heapifies — yielding O(log N) per assignment instead of O(N) linear scan. If the root reaches zero capacity it is removed automatically.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Core.Collections.SingleFlightCache<TKey, TValue>
files.Summary: A thread-safe, fixed-TTL cache of asynchronous reads in which every caller asking for the same key while a read is in flight shares that one read.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Core.Collections.TimedCache<TKey, TValue>
files.Summary:
A thread-safe, write-through TTL cache where entries expire after a fixed duration from when they were stored. Reads do NOT extend the lifetime (unlike ).

Supports bounded head-first for memory management.

Ages are measured on , not the host's wall clock. A TTL is a duration, and on DateTime.UtcNow a clock stepped back an hour kept every entry "fresh" for that hour: the world server's available-scene cache served the same instance list, populations and all, long after the instances had filled or gone.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.IAccountCreationPuzzleProvider
files.Summary:
Scaffold interface for client-side proof-of-work (PoW) puzzles issued during account creation. The global hourly cap (maxGlobalAccountCreationsPerHour) absorbs the impact of registration floods, but spending the budget still costs the server real database I/O. A small PoW puzzle (e.g. a SHA-256 difficulty challenge) shifts the cost asymmetry: an attacker pays CPU per attempt while a legitimate user pays only milliseconds.

The intended production implementation:

  • Server issues a (challenge, difficulty) tuple bound to the handshake nonce and connection,
  • Client solves and returns a nonce such that H(challenge || nonce) has the required leading zero bits,
  • Server verifies in <1ms and proceeds with account creation.

The puzzle MUST be bound to the connection / handshake to prevent pre-mining a stockpile of valid solutions. Difficulty is increased dynamically when the global cap is approaching saturation.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.AccountVerificationPolicy
files.Summary:
Single source of truth for whether, and on which channels, new accounts must prove their contact details: the development-only AutoVerifyAccounts bypass and the per-channel VerifyEmail / VerifySms / VerifyDiscord switches. Which codes an account is then sent and asked for is AccountVerificationRules, shared with the Control Panel.

Two call sites must agree on these answers:

  • Account creation, which decides which codes to send and whether to verify the account outright.
  • The login lookup, which otherwise rejects an unverified account. Without the login side honouring the same switches, an account created before a switch changed would be asked for a code no server will ever send, or let in without one it still owes.

Precedence, highest first.

  1. AutoVerifyAccounts=true (editor and development builds only): every account is verified at creation and no code is sent.
  2. VerifyEmail / VerifySms / VerifyDiscord say which channels this server sends codes on. When all three are false, every new account is verified at creation through the same database write the bypass uses.
  3. Otherwise a code goes out on each channel the player chose that is switched on and the account can receive, falling back to email; any one code verifies the account, and there is no grace period: sign-in asks for a code until one is entered.

The compile-time guard on is deliberate: a production player build ignores that key entirely, so a Development LoginServer.cfg that leaks into a production deployment cannot re-enable the bypass. Consequently the flag also has no effect in a server binary built with the Production working environment — build the server with the Development working environment for local testing. The channel switches have no such guard; a missing or unreadable value counts as true, so a typo verifies more, never less.

None of this decides two-factor. An authenticator is set up when the player opts in at registration, however the account was verified, on the game and the Control Panel alike.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.AsyncWorkerData
files.Summary:
Centralized async work queue.

Replaces fire-and-forget _ = SomeAsync(...) across all server systems with a bounded, backpressure-aware pool that runs work items concurrently while preserving FIFO order between items that share an entity key.

Design:

  • Work runs concurrently, capped by . A slow item delays only the items ordered behind it.
  • Items sharing an entityKey run in the order they were enqueued, one at a time.
  • Bounded admission: returns false once items are accepted but unfinished.
  • Nothing ever executes on the calling thread — see .

Usage:

// Unordered — runs as soon as a concurrency slot is free:
asyncWorkerData.Enqueue(() => PersistInventoryAsync(dto));

// Ordered — this character's items run in enqueue order, one at a time:
asyncWorkerData.Enqueue(() => SaveCharacterAsync(charData), characterID);

Systems declare dependency via: [RequiresDataContainer(typeof(AsyncWorkerData))]

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.LoginServer.LoginQueueSystem
files.Summary:
Manages a FIFO login queue for clients arriving when the server is at authentication capacity. Queued clients stay connected at the QUIC layer and receive periodic position updates via . When admitted (position reaches 0), the client re-initiates the handshake and proceeds through normal authentication.

Update rate: The LoginQueueUpdateRateSeconds config key controls how often position updates are broadcast. This is server-authoritative only — clients cannot request faster updates.

Admission rate: Clients are admitted from the queue at a server-configured rate (LoginQueueAdmissionRatePerSecond) to prevent the newly-admitted clients from immediately re-saturating auth capacity.

When it engages: only when a handshake would push the number of connections mid-authentication past the authenticator's pending cap (AuthMaxPendingConnections, default 1,000 on the login server: what its SRP verify and proof channels hold between them, see PendingAuthRules.DefaultLoginPendingCap). The authenticator finds this system in the behaviour registry when it needs it, so the system has to be listed in the LoginServer scene's behaviours for the queue to exist at all.

Threading: main thread only. Every entry point is reached from a FishNet callback, the authenticator's handshake path or its per-frame sweep, all of which run on the main thread.

Shared utility for main-thread queue drain and enqueue operations. Eliminates copy-paste boilerplate across server systems (D1).

Back-pressure observability: the underlying enforces a hard capacity cap (currently 10,000 pending actions) and returns false from TryEnqueue when full. Most call sites discard that bool because there is no useful off-thread fallback — the response broadcast is already on the main thread by contract. To keep the loss visible to operators, every rejected enqueue is counted here in a per-queue-type drop counter and surfaced through a rate-limited warning. A sustained non-zero drop rate indicates the main thread is stalling long enough for async DB workers to saturate the queue (10K * 16 ms drain budget ≈ several seconds of hang) and is a stronger DoS / GC-pause signal than any individual client time-out.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.UnitySyncOverAsync
files.Summary:
Blocks the calling thread on an async operation without risking a deadlock.

Unity installs a UnitySynchronizationContext on the main thread; continuations posted to it only run when the player loop drains them. Any await in the callee that captures that context — i.e. any await without ConfigureAwait(false), anywhere in the call chain — can therefore never resume while the main thread sits in GetResult()/.Result/.Wait(). The server then stays alive but never finishes InitializeOnce, so the transport never binds its port.

Shutdown paths only. OnDestroy/OnApplicationQuit cannot yield and the process exits immediately afterwards, so there is no continuation to hand work to — a bounded block is the only way to flush pending state before exit. Startup has no such constraint and must not use this: behaviours initialize through ServerBehaviour.InitializeOnceAsync, driven by Server's initialization coroutine, which leaves the main thread free to drain continuations.

Where a bounded block genuinely is required, route it through here rather than hand-rolling Task.Run(...).Wait(...): call sites should not have to audit an entire EF/Npgsql call chain to know whether blocking is safe.

files.Summary:
Abstract base class for all behavior tree nodes. Nodes are ScriptableObject assets so designers can build trees entirely in the Unity inspector without code.

Behavior trees sit above the state machine layer and decide which the NPC should transition to. The state machine then handles the actual movement, combat, and animation logic.

Node types:

  • — Tries children left-to-right, returns first success.
  • — Runs children left-to-right, fails on first failure.
  • — Inverts the child's result.
  • — Repeats the child a configurable number of times.
  • — Leaf that checks an .
  • — Leaf that transitions to a .

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.World.SceneServer.AI.AIBehaviorTree
files.Summary:
Root container for a behavior tree. Assign to to give an NPC high-level decision-making above the state machine.

The tree is evaluated once per AI tick (governed by AI LOD). If the root node returns , the tree produced a state transition and the current state's UpdateState is skipped for that tick. If it returns , the current state continues normally.

Example tree: 

AIBehaviorTree (root = Selector)
  ├─ Sequence: [Condition: IsDead] → [StateTransition: DeadState]
  ├─ Sequence: [Condition: HP ≤ 30%] → [StateTransition: RetreatState]
  ├─ Sequence: [Condition: EnemyNearby] → [StateTransition: AttackState]
  └─ StateTransition: WanderState

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.World.SceneServer.AI.AggressionState
files.Summary:
Manages the aggression (threat) system for a single NPC. Owns the instance, subscribes to global damage/heal/kill events, and tracks the per-NPC target re-evaluation timer.

Extracted from to keep the controller focused on navigation and state management. One instance per NPC — plain C# class.

Event-driven combat entry: every hit this NPC takes is reported through , and the brain decides from its own state whether that hit starts a fight (). It used to fire only when the table went from empty to non-empty, and nothing but a kill ever emptied it: a fight that ended any other way — the target out of reach, zoned, leashed away — left entries behind, so every later hit from beyond the detection radius was recorded and ignored, and each one refreshed the entry that kept it from ever going stale. Deciding per hit from the brain's state has no edge to consume.

Replay safety: Event handlers are guarded to ignore damage/heal/kill events fired during prediction replay. Global combat events are not replay-suppressed by the damage controller, so we suppress them here.

files.Title: FishMMO.Server.Implementation.World.SceneServer.AI.BossScript
files.Summary:
ScriptableObject that defines a boss encounter's phases and timed mechanics. Assign to to make an NPC a scripted boss.

The evaluates the boss script every tick:

  1. Checks health against phase thresholds.
  2. On phase change, applies overrides (behavior tree, attacking state, ability rotation) and spawns adds.
  3. Ticks all active timed mechanics and force-activates abilities or spawns when timers fire.

Example setup: 

Phases:
  [0] HP ≥ 70%  — default behavior
  [1] HP < 70%  — spawn 2 adds, switch to Phase2 behavior tree
  [2] HP < 40%  — enrage: switch to melee attacking state

Timed Mechanics:
Meteor — every 30s, force-cast AbilityTemplate #5
Summon — every 60s, spawn skeleton prefab (only in phase 1)

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.AbilityActivationFlags
files.Summary:
Flags representing the activation state of an ability. Stored as bit positions in an int and manipulated via IntBitExtensions.

Bit position 0 (IsActualData) is used as a sentinel to distinguish real input from FishNet's default-filled replicate data. Data without this bit set does NOT stop the replicate: AbilityController.ReplicateInternal clears the queued ability, carries the held flag over from the replicated state, and goes on simulating — a tick with no new input still has to advance an active cast, its cooldowns and its resource drain, or the owner and the server diverge whenever a packet is late. This lets bit 0 double as a "data present" marker without consuming an extra field in the replicate struct.

Constraint: All enum values are bit positions and must remain in the range 0–15 (bits 0–15 after shifting). stores flags in the lower 16 bits. Values at or above 16 will be silently truncated during reconcile.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ApplyDamageAction
files.Summary:
Action that applies damage to a target character using a configurable value provider and a given damage attribute type.

Runs on the server, and on the client that OWNS the initiator — see . The caster draws its own number immediately through rather than waiting half a round trip for the server's report; the server's report then confirms it, or the prediction is greyed out when none arrives. Observers still wait to be told.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ApplyReviveAction
files.Summary:
Action that offers a resurrect to a dead target character. Unlike , this applies to dead characters (CurrentValue == 0). Used by resurrect/resurrection ability templates.

For a player with a live connection this sends a and stops there — the death dialog surfaces its "Accept Resurrect" button and the player chooses between that and respawning at their bind point. The revive itself happens in CharacterSystem's accept handler, which is the only place that both clears and restores health.

A target that cannot be asked — an NPC, or a player with no active connection — is revived outright, so scripted and system resurrects still work.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.AttributeBuffTemplate
files.Summary: Buff template that grants bonus attributes to a character while active. Applies additive modifiers on apply/stack and removes them symmetrically on remove/unstack.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.AttributeReconcileEntry
files.Summary:
A single non-resource character attribute entry for reconcile serialization. Mirrors / index-delta compression so unchanged attributes contribute zero network bytes.

Resource attributes (HP/MP/Stamina) are NOT carried by this entry — they ride on the reconcile payload because they also need CurrentValue + RegenTickAccum state that base attributes do not have.

Only (authoritative base) and (sum of buff / equipment / region contributions) are reconciled. FormulaModifier is intentionally recomputed locally via the dependency graph (CharacterAttribute.ApplyChildren): replicating it would (a) cost bandwidth for a derived value and (b) potentially overwrite a more up-to-date local computation.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.AttributeTickBuffTemplate
files.Summary: Buff template that applies cumulative attribute modifiers on each tick. Each tick adds a modifier; on remove, the total accumulated modifier is reversed. Tracks total applied ticks internally on the buff to ensure perfect symmetry. Useful for "ramping" buffs that grow stronger over time.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.AuthSizeLimits

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.BakedSceneData

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.BuffReconcileEntry

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.CharacterAttributeResourceStateSerializer
files.Summary:
Custom serializers for .

Regular serializer (Write/Read extension methods): Used by FishNet's codegen for RPCs, SyncVars, broadcasts, and any non-prediction serialization context. Writes every field using FishNet's built-in packed encoding (varint for ints, full precision for floats).

Delta serializer (registered via /): Used during prediction replicate/reconcile ticks. Writes a 2-byte bitmask (one bit per field) followed by delta-encoded values for only the changed fields. On a typical tick where only health regens, this sends ~4-5 bytes instead of 40.

The delta serializer must use because FishNet's [DefaultDeltaWriter] attribute only supports single-value signatures, not the (prev, next, option) signature needed for per-field delta compression.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.CharacterReconcileDataDeltaSerializer
files.Summary:
Custom delta serializers for .

Delta serializer: Writes a 2-byte bitmask (13 bits for 13 fields) followed by delta-encoded values for only the changed fields. The nested and use their own delta serializers, so savings compound. Cooldowns, buffs, and non-resource attributes use index-delta compression via , , and .

Who owns what (FishNet delta prediction, FISHNET_DELTA_PREDICTION). FishNet writes every reconcile behind a one-byte header (a full flag plus a 7-bit id of the full reconcile a delta was written against). A FULL reconcile — the first one, one per observer added, and one every min(TickRate, 60) ticks — goes through the REGULAR serializer, . Every other reconcile goes through with RootSerialize, as a delta against the last FULL reconcile as readers decoded it, not against the previous reconcile. The reader only uses a delta when it holds the full reconcile that delta names, and otherwise decodes it to stay aligned and discards it. Loss detection and late-joiner bootstrap are therefore FishNet's, which is why this serializer no longer carries the mode byte and chain sequence it needed when the fork chained each delta onto the previous one.

The contract this serializer keeps for FishNet: write bytes if and only if it returns true; always write something at RootSerialize; consume the same number of bytes whatever baseline the reader holds (a rejected delta is still decoded); never modify the baseline instance, which is reused for every delta until the next full reconcile — the array readers copy before they patch.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.CharacterReplicateDataDeltaSerializer
files.Summary:
Custom delta serializers for .

Delta serializer: Writes a 1-byte bitmask followed by delta-encoded values for only the changed fields. All eight bits are in use — bit 3 opens a second byte for the rare one-shot fields (equipment request, convergence distance, hit claim), see the constants.

An idle tick costs the bitmask alone. For real figures rather than an estimate, run PredictionBandwidthBenchmarkTests, which measures this type against the production serializers; byte counts written into a comment go stale the first time a field is added.

Custom delta serializers for .

Delta serializer: Writes a 1-byte bitmask (6 bits for 6 fields) followed by delta-encoded values for only the changed fields. When the grounding status is stable and unchanged this writer declines entirely and sends NOTHING — the parent's flags word records its absence. It only emits a bitmask when something changed, or when a caller forces it, and nothing forces it today: FishNet writes a full reconcile with the regular serializer and hands the delta writers only RootSerialize, which the root reconcile turns into Unset for its fields.

A trigger executes a list of actions against a set of targets selected by , branching on whether are satisfied for each selected target.

Lifecycle (per fire):

  2. yields N targets (using / as context).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.DeterministicRNG
files.Summary:
A fast, deterministic, thread-safe pseudo-random number generator. Drop-in replacement for in all game code.

Algorithm: xoshiro128** (Blackman & Vigna, 2018). Period: 2^128 − 1. Passes BigCrush. Thread safety: no shared mutable state — each instance is independent.

API surface matches the subset of used in this codebase: Next(), Next(int), Next(int,int), NextDouble(), NextFloat(), Range(int,int), Range(float,float).

A static instance is provided for fire-and-forget usage that does not require determinism (replaces UnityEngine.Random).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.DynamicAddressableLoadPathSystem
files.Summary:
Dynamically overrides the Addressables remote load path at runtime. Registers a persistent InternalIdTransformFunc on the Addressables ResourceManager that rewrites remote asset URLs to use RuntimeBaseUrl. Only one instance should exist in the scene — the last one to Awake wins.

Client builds with an empty or loopback RuntimeBaseUrl do not register a rewrite: Addressables.RuntimePath already resolves correctly (including WebGL, where StreamingAssets is an absolute http(s) URL derived from the page origin, e.g. https://fishmmo.com/test/StreamingAssets/aa). Rewriting those IDs to a hardcoded host (or prefixing file://) breaks loads when the game is served from a different domain or subpath.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.EquipmentController
files.Summary:
Controls the character's equipment slots, handling equip/unequip logic and network synchronization.

Implements at Order 93 so equipment participates in the prediction pipeline: an owner's equip or unequip is INPUT, carried by , applied by both the owner and the server inside the replicate body for that tick, and confirmed by the reconcile. Equipment-driven attribute changes therefore land on the same tick on both peers, and the attribute reconcile (Order 95) never has a socket to correct that the replay would not also have re-applied.

Three network paths feed this container and they must agree with one another:

  • The spawn payload (/) — owner shaped for the owner, template+seed only for everyone else.
  • The owner's replicate input and reconcile snapshot: the input moves items, the snapshot says which instance sits in each socket, and settles any disagreement by MOVING the real instance, never by cloning it. A reconcile that predates a request restores the earlier state and the replay re-applies the request.
  • , sent by the server to the character's observers after every successful equip/unequip, applied by .

Manages visual equipment rendering on a character. Pre-allocates renderers per slot, loads equipment prefabs via Addressables, extracts meshes and materials, binds skinned meshes to the character skeleton, and coordinates body region hiding with .

All rendering operations are client-only, guarded with #if !UNITY_SERVER. Public API and interface implementations exist unconditionally for server compilation.

files.Summary:
Selects the already carried on the event — without running any spatial query. This is the intended default for triggers fired in response to an event that already resolved its own target, such as:

  • Ability OnHit triggers (collision target).
  • Region enter / exit triggers.
  • Dialogue, item-use, or interaction triggers.

Falls back to the initiator's GameObject when the event has no Target — so an OnHit trigger fired as a self-cast (initiator == hit) still resolves correctly.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.HostConfig
files.Summary:
IL-embedded host configuration.

The defaults here are sentinels, and this file is tracked so the project always compiles. The real values live in the gitignored HostConfig.generated.cs, written by FishMMO Dashboard > Game Settings (or by CI substituting the sentinels in GeneratedFileTemplates/HostConfig.generated.cs.template), which implements to overwrite them.

Why the split: a fresh clone has no generated file. When the generated file declared the whole class, its absence was a compile error, and a project that fails to compile on first open drops into Safe Mode, where no editor code runs — including the FishMMO menu that writes the file. An unimplemented partial method is removed by the compiler, so a missing generated file now just means sentinels, which ClientSecurityBuildValidator refuses to ship.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.KCCMoveFlags
files.Summary:
Flags representing movement actions for KCC input replication. Used as a bitmask for jump, crouch, sprint, and other actions.

One-shot vs. continuous flags: is a one-shot impulse that should fire once and be cleared. and are continuous (held) flags that persist while the key is held.

This used to add "observer prediction clears one-shot flags to prevent indefinite re-prediction. When adding new one-shot flags, include them in OneShotMask." There is no OneShotMask and there never was one in this project, and the clearing it described belonged to the observer-prediction path — which does not run: state forwarding is off, so FishNet never invokes a replicate body on a non-owner. A one-shot flag is cleared by its producer, KCCPlayer.PopulateInput, on the tick after it is consumed.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.KinematicCharacterMotorStateDeltaSerializer
files.Summary:
Custom delta serializers for .

Delta serializer: Writes a 2-byte bitmask over 16 bit positions carrying 15 fields and an extension (bit 4, once a retired gap — see the constants below: a further byte of flags for the climbing fields, sent only on a tick one of them changes) followed by delta-encoded values for only the changed fields. On a typical grounded walking tick, only Position, Rotation, BaseVelocity, and GroundingStatus change. On an idle tick where the character stands still this writer declines and sends nothing at all. Measured figures live in PredictionBandwidthBenchmarkTests rather than here, where they cannot go stale silently.

The nested uses its own delta serializer, so savings compound for unchanged grounding normals.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.LoginQueuePositionBroadcast
files.Summary:
Broadcast sent by the LoginServer to a queued client with their current position in the login queue. Sent periodically at a server-configured rate.

Position semantics:

  • > 0 — Waiting in queue. Display the position to the user.
  • 0 — Admitted. The client should re-initiate the handshake now.
  • -1 — Cancelled. The queue entry was purged (timeout or shutdown).

Server-authoritative update rate: The server controls how often this broadcast is sent via the LoginQueueUpdateRateSeconds config key. Clients are passive receivers only — there is no request path for faster updates.

Validation: The server MUST enforce the documented QueuePosition semantics (>0 waiting, 0 admitted, -1 cancelled). The client treats these values as authoritative — no local defensive validation is performed.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.NameGeneration.StableHash
files.Summary:
Cross-process-stable hashing used for deterministic seed derivation.

These helpers produce the same value across processes, runtimes, and platforms for the same input bytes.

Algorithm: FNV-1a over UTF-8 bytes.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.NamedSceneObjectTargetSelector
files.Summary:
Resolves a scene by name at runtime. Designed for asset-based Triggers that need to point at a specific scene object — selectors serialized on ScriptableObject assets cannot hold direct scene references, but they can hold a name string and look the object up when the trigger fires.

The lookup is scoped to the context's scene (whatever scene the event's Target or Initiator lives in). If no scene context is available, the active scene is used. Names are compared exactly (case sensitive). For non-unique names, use instead, or compose this selector with per-target conditions to disambiguate.

Performance: the lookup walks the scene's root objects and their descendants on every fire. For frequent triggers, cache the resolved GameObject in your scene wiring rather than depending on a name lookup.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PointOfInterestOutline
files.Summary: A site's footprint seen from above (2026-10-18: "Towns, cities and all other points of interest need different carving besides just circles"): how far its ground reaches from its anchor toward each of a ring of evenly spaced bearings, the first due north (+z), turning east (+x) as a yaw does. Between two bearings its edge runs straight, so the footprint is a star-shaped polygon: every point of it is seen from the anchor, and a ray from the anchor leaves it exactly once.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PointOfInterestPad

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PointOfInterestTerraces
files.Summary: A pad's terraces (2026-10-18: hill towns): its ground levelled not to one height but to two to four, stepped up the fall line like a hillside's fields, with an earth bank between each pair and a ramp up every bank where a street climbs.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PointOfInterestTraits

files.Summary: The local player's view of which portals are open, per scene, as the server last reported it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PortalRegistry

files.Summary: The face of a scene teleporter: a quad in its opening that shows the place it leads to. Both scenes cannot be loaded at once, so the view is a cubemap baked at the destination (PortalViewBaker, kept in Assets/Generated and shipped in a build-only Addressables group), looked up through the quad by view direction in the FishMMO/Portal shader: a window onto the far side with the right perspective for anything past a few metres, a swirl and a glowing rim over it. With no baked view (an editor that has not baked, a destination not yet set) only the glow shows.

files.Summary: A portal's world-wide opening: for good, or until a moment.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PredictedAbilityStateHistory
files.Summary: Per-tick record of what the owning client predicted for its ability controller, so a reconcile can be compared against the client's state at the reconcile tick rather than against whatever the client holds now.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PredictedCombatEvents.Kind
files.Summary: What a predicted entry describes.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PredictedRushStops

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PredictionHealth
files.Summary: The client's own prediction health over the last minute: how often the server corrected its movement by more than a centimetre, and what share of the hits it predicted the server rejected. Shown in the network overlay; the numbers every prediction fix is measured by.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PredictionTick
files.Summary: A tick value that can only be legitimately produced from a replicate input via . Because the constructor is internal, callers outside this assembly cannot construct one from a raw uint (e.g. TimeManager.LocalTick) without an explicit, intentional conversion — the compiler enforces correct tick sourcing on every Apply() call in the prediction path.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PremadeAbilityTemplate
files.Summary: A complete, ready-to-use ability a merchant sells: a base with its events already chosen, at a price of its own.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PropChunkLedger.Hold

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PropChunkLedger
files.Summary: Which of one scene's prop collision chunks are wanted, kept by reference count: every focus point holds the chunks round the 32 m cell it stands in, and a chunk is wanted while any focus holds it. The bookkeeping half of , with no Unity objects in it, so it is testable on its own.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.PropColliderStreamer
files.Summary: Puts a scene's baked prop collision into physics only where something can touch it: within of every character on the server, and within of the camera on the client. A chunk ( square) at a time, as one mesh: every collidable prop in it merged and cooked off the main thread, then handed to one static collider.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RaceProportions
files.Summary: Default body proportions for a race. These values are applied as bone scaling on character spawn. 1.0 = default human proportion. Values are multipliers on individual bone localScale.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RaceTemplate
files.Summary: ScriptableObject template for a race: models, attributes, starting abilities, inventory and equipment for playable races, and the naming data the name generator draws on for every race. A race with off exists only to name things — it has no prefab or models, is skipped by character creation, and loads no placeholder model.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RandomRangeFloatValue
files.Summary: Float value provider that returns a random float between and (inclusive). Uses the deterministic from when available, otherwise falls back to .

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RandomRangeValue
files.Summary: Value provider that returns a random integer between and (inclusive). Uses the deterministic from when available, otherwise falls back to .

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RandomTargetSelector
files.Summary: Selects a random from all within a given radius and layer mask. Useful for random targeting effects or abilities.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.Region
files.Summary:
Represents a networked region in the game world. Handles region hierarchy, collider setup, and triggers region actions on player entry, stay, and exit.

Membership is tracked locally in a rather than trusting the NetworkCollider callbacks one-for-one: FishNet re-polls colliders during prediction reconcile replay (and we deliberately fire nothing while a character teleports), so callbacks that arrive while suppressed are recorded only and the resulting Enter/Exit is raised exactly once on the next non-reconciling post-tick via a raw-vs-effective diff. Stay never fires during replay.

Hierarchy: a child region takes ownership of a character standing inside it. Every ancestor receives a paired Exit only if it had raised an Enter, and a parent re-Enters when the last child releases the character while it is still physically inside the parent. Parent Stay is suppressed while any descendant owns the character.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RegionActionGate
files.Summary: Authority gate for region actions that mutate gameplay state (buffs, attributes). The server is authoritative for gameplay; clients only observe the result through the normal replication/reconcile path, so these actions must never run on a client peer.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RegionEventData
files.Summary: ECA event data for region-related triggers. Carries the Region reference and whether the FishNet prediction system is currently reconciling.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RegionGeometry
files.Summary: Point-containment helpers for region colliders. Axis-aligned Collider.bounds is wrong for rotated boxes, so boxes are tested in their own local space; other convex colliders use ; anything else falls back to bounds.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RegionMembership<T>
files.Summary:
Pure, engine-free bookkeeping for which characters a considers "inside". Separates the two truths a region has to reconcile:

  • Raw presence: what the underlying NetworkCollider has told us via Enter/Exit callbacks. This is updated on every callback, including during prediction reconcile replay and while a character is teleporting.
  • Effective membership: characters for which the region has actually raised an Enter (and no Exit yet). Gameplay/visual triggers key off this set.

Callbacks that arrive while suppressed (reconciling or teleporting) update raw presence only; later diffs raw against effective and yields the Enter/Exit decisions that were deferred, each exactly once. Because is a pure diff it also repairs any drift between the two sets (e.g. a child region releasing a character back to its parent).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RemoveItemAction
files.Summary: ECA action that removes items from a character's inventory by template. Server-only execution.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RemovedItemRecord
files.Summary: One vacated inventory slot, recorded for the persistence layer before the container forgot it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RenewTokenResponseBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast sent by a World or Scene server immediately after a successful authentication, carrying a freshly-minted auth token with a refreshed expiration window. The client decrypts the new token over the existing AES-GCM session channel and replaces its stored token so that future reconnects continue working past the original LoginServer-issued token's expiration.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestConnectionTokenBroadcast
files.Summary: Client → server: request a connection token for the server this client is about to connect to next (Login → World, World → Scene).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestInitialSceneBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast requesting the initial scene to be loaded for the client. No additional data required.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestInstanceDetailsBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast asking the server for the state of the instance the character is standing in.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestLeaveInstanceBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast asking the server to remove the character from its current instance and return it to the open world.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestSceneChannelListBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast requesting the list of available scene channels from the server. Sent by the client to request an updated channel list for the current scene.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RequestServerListBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast for requesting the list of available servers. No additional data required.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RescuePoint
files.Summary: One place a rescue can send a character to.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RescuePointKind
files.Summary: The kinds of authored place a character can be rescued to.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RescuePoints
files.Summary: Reads the places a character can be rescued to out of a scene's cached details.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ResourceConsumableTemplate
files.Summary: A consumable that restores resources: a healing potion, a mana draught, a ration.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ResourceRestoration
files.Summary: One resource an item restores, and by how much.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ResourceTickBuffTemplate
files.Summary: Buff template that applies periodic resource modifications (heal-over-time / damage-over-time). Each tick adds or subtracts from the current value of target resource attributes. The tick amount scales linearly with the number of stacks (base + stacks). This buff is deterministic — identical inputs produce identical state changes.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RespawnAtBindPointBroadcast
files.Summary: Sent client to server when the dead player chooses to respawn at their bind point.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ResurrectAcceptBroadcast
files.Summary: Sent client to server when the dead player accepts a resurrect.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ResurrectOfferBroadcast
files.Summary: Sent server to client when another player offers a resurrect. The client adds an "Accept Resurrect" button to the death dialog.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ReverseNamingBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast for looking up an entity by name in the naming system. Contains the type, lowercase name, ID, and original name.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RevokeTokenBroadcast
files.Summary:
Broadcast sent by the client during an explicit logout to ask the LoginServer to revoke its currently-held auth token before its TTL expires. The token is sent as the raw HMAC-signed bytes the LoginServer originally issued (and which the client decrypted into memory on SrpSuccess). The server hashes the bytes via TokenService.HashToken and matches the row in IAuthTokenService.

Security note: this broadcast is sent over the FishNet transport without additional encryption; the server's AES-GCM auth channel has typically been torn down by the time the user logs out. Because the only purpose is to revoke the token the eavesdropper would have captured anyway, this is safe.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RewindTarget
files.Summary: A point in the past to rewind the world to: a whole tick, plus how far before that tick the target actually sits.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.RichText
files.Summary: Utility class for formatting rich text strings with color, size, and optional prefixes/suffixes for UI display. Provides both string-returning Format methods and zero-allocation AppendTo methods for StringBuilder use.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneBackdrop
files.Summary: The terrain around a generated scene, out to the horizon: drawn, never walked on.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneBoundary
files.Summary: MonoBehaviour for defining a scene boundary. Draws gizmos for visualization and provides boundary size and offset.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneBoundaryDetails
files.Summary: Serializable class containing details for a scene boundary, including origin, size, and point containment logic.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneBoundaryDictionary
files.Summary: Serializable dictionary mapping string keys to scene boundary details. Provides logic to check if a point is contained in any boundary.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveForm
files.Summary: The kind of cave a spot is in, which says what can live there (the cut's cave forms, by the same ordinals).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveLife.Set
files.Summary: One scene's spots, as offered.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveLife
files.Summary: The cave-life spots of every loaded scene (), keyed by scene, offered by the scene's client-only site emitters () while it is loaded: what the ambient life places its cave creatures from.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveLifeFlags
files.Summary: What else a cave-life spot is (bits).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveLifeKind
files.Summary: What a cave-life spot is: the kind of place in a cave an animal lives on, in or over.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveLifeSpot
files.Summary: One place in a carved cave its animals live at, baked by the cut from the cave's own field (the cave dressing): a flat patch of floor, wall or roof, a box of clear air, a pool, a mouth. The ambient life places its cave creatures on these and keeps them to them, so it needs no ray against the cave's rock, and the cave's floors under and over each other are no puzzle to it (the terrain's one height a place is useless underground).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveMeshes.Cave
files.Summary: One cave system's meshes, as last built.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveMeshes
files.Summary: The main object of a scene's <Scene> Caves.asset: its cave systems' rock meshes are sub-assets of it (Cave <site id> P<n>, stored unreadable, each with its collider Cave <site id> C<n>: the same triangles on positions alone, since 2026-10-20), and it keeps, per cave, the key of the inputs those meshes were built from, so a repaint or re-cut that changes nothing about a cave keeps its meshes instead of building them again.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCaveWater
files.Summary: What lives on and in a cave's still water as every client draws it (2026-10-26, phase I2n-c; decision 86 (i) and its leeches, decision 97): marsh-gas BEADS rising in trails from the drowned muck and ringing out on the surface, and LEECHES swimming in it, toward whoever wades in. Pure; FishCaveWaterLife.shader mirrors it number for number (CaveWaterLife draws it).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneChannelListBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast for sending a list of available scene channels to the client. Contains a list of channel addresses.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneChannelSelectBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast for selecting a specific scene channel. Contains the selected channel address.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneClimbable
files.Summary: One ladder, rope ladder or rope a character can climb, baked by the cut (a cave's shafts and ledges, a mine's levels): the climbing movement mode, the server's NavMesh links and the NPCs' traversal of them all read these, nothing else. The pieces drawn for it are baked props, data like this, so nothing here refers to them.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneClimbableKind
files.Summary: What a climbable is, which sets how fast it is climbed and whether a climber can shuffle across it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneClimbables
files.Summary: The climbables of every loaded scene (), keyed by scene and filed by horizontal cell, for the climbing movement mode (both peers) and the server's NavMesh links.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCloudWorld.Crossing
files.Summary: A rope bridge between two islands: its end posts' feet, where the walk meets the grass at each end.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCloudWorld.Dock
files.Summary: A landing stage at an island's edge, where airships tie up: its end over the void, and the way out.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCloudWorld.Island
files.Summary: One floating island: its outline's centre and reach, and the height of its ground.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCloudWorld.IslandKind
files.Summary: What an island is for: how big it was planned, and so what the cut put on it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneCloudWorld
files.Summary: A scene cut on a gas giant (Celestial.CloudWorld): islands of rock floating over a cloud deck with nothing under it. Written by the cut, kept by the server and every client, and found by scene () by what has to know: the sky (the deck it draws below the islands), the server (who has fallen into it), the airships (the docks they sail between).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneContentLoads.Load
files.Summary: One fetch in flight.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneContentLoads.Work
files.Summary: Work a system still has to do on content that has arrived before the world looks finished (grass taking its terrains, props merging into pools). Polled, not counted: it is added once and asked each frame the loading screen is up.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneContentLoads
files.Summary: The content a scene fetches for itself after it has loaded: its terrain arrays, biome templates, river flow and the like, each an Addressable load a component starts from its own lifecycle. Those run outside the scene load and outside 's batches, so nothing that waits on either sees them. The client's loading screen holds world entry until this is empty, so the player arrives in a finished world instead of watching ground and water arrive from the cache or the web server.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneDrip
files.Summary: Water dripping from a cave's roof (2026-10-20, caves livened; ): how often a drip falls, how its drops fall, when each lands, and how its seed carries the puddle under it. One definition read by the client's drops and puddle rings (CaveDrips and its shader, which repeats , and the ring constants), its sound (CaveDripPresenter) and the cave dressing that bakes the drips.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneDripLanding
files.Summary: What a drip's drops land on (bits 27–28 of a 's seed). Append only: stored in scene assets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneEmitter
files.Summary: One place in a scene that gives off smoke or light, baked by the cut from the pieces its sites laid: the client's site lights and hearth smoke read these, nothing else (SceneSiteEmitters).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneEmitterKind
files.Summary: What a site's piece gives off where it stands (StructurePieces.EmittersOf).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneGlow
files.Summary: The cold glow of faerie, rune and crystal light (2026-10-18, I6g; ): its tint, its soft slow pulse and when it shows. One definition read by the client's site lights (SiteLightPool) and, constant for constant, by the glowing parts of the pieces that give it off (FishStructureWeathering.hlsl FishStructureGlowLight), so a rune stone's runes brighten and dim with the light they cast.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneGlowCave
files.Summary: One linked cave as the glow modes read it (2026-10-26, phase I2n-c, decision 86 (h)): the box of its air (the union of its cave-life spots, padded) and the glow table's row of the interior biome dressing its inside, so a crystal or a glow-worm colony in it moves by the INTERIOR's glow mode (an EYELID, …) and not by the host land's over it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneGlowCaves
files.Summary: The linked caves' boxes the glow modes read (pure; the GPU's FishGlowCaveRow mirrors ): found from the cave-life spots every client loads (: each spot of a linked cave carries its interior biome), so nothing new is stored. A glow whose origin is inside a box reads the box's row before any anchor disc or the biome grid.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneGlowHue
files.Summary: The cool tints a is made in (bits 8–10 of its seed). Append only: stored in scene assets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneLoadBroadcast
files.Summary: Broadcast for loading a specific scene. Contains the name of the scene to load.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneMagma
files.Summary: The molten lava of a lava tube that still runs (2026-10-20; and ): its light's colour and slow churn, how its seed carries the body under it, how much it sparks, the hot air over it and the haze under the roof. One definition read by the client's site lights (SiteLightPool), its embers and fumes (SiteEmbers), its heat haze (the heat shimmer) and the cave walk render.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneMagmaBody
files.Summary: What body of molten lava a stands over (bits 24–25 of its seed). Append only: stored in scene assets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneNames
files.Summary: A loaded scene's name without the garbage: builds a new string on every read, and the render hooks that seed their placement from it (ambient and sea life, sea floats, the glow sky's episodes) read it every frame.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneObject
files.Summary: Manages registration and tracking of scene objects with unique IDs in FishMMO.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneObjectNamer
files.Summary:
Gives a scene object a generated name — a character, city, dungeon, point of interest or legendary item name — from the name generator, using the object's race and the settings authored on the prefab.

The server rolls a seed and a gender and ships those (4 + 1 bytes); every peer then regenerates the same name from the same templates, so the name itself never crosses the wire. The race comes from the object's unless the settings override it, which is how one prefab names itself correctly at any spawner.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneObjectNames
files.Summary: The installed scene object name source; null without the Naming module, when every object keeps its authored name.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneObjectNamingMode
files.Summary: Which generator a draws its name from.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneObjectNamingSettings
files.Summary: Everything a designer sets on a . Authored on the prefab, so it is identical on both peers and never travels over the wire.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePath
files.Summary: One way through a scene: a polyline on the finished ground with its width, wear and surface along it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathClass
files.Summary: What kind of way a path is: how wide, what it is made of, how steep it may climb and how hard it is kept.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathField
files.Summary: A scene's paths rasterised for the GPU: a distance field half a metre a texel, kept only in the 16 m pages a path passes through. What the terrain, the grass and the details read to draw, thin and clear a path (FishGroundPaths.hlsl).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathForm
files.Summary: How a way runs (, 2026-10-26, phase I2l-b; decisions 50, 56, 87): routed round the ground as every way was, or one of the straight roads, with the profile it is built to. Append only; the ordinal is stored in scene assets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathPointFlags
files.Summary: Per-point facts about a path ().

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathStyle
files.Summary: A path class's numbers: its width, surface and kept-ness; how steep it may climb and how it meets the ground.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathSurface
files.Summary: What a stretch of path is surfaced with. The shader reads it as a code ().

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePathSurfaceBinder
files.Summary: Hands the GPU a scene's paths: the page table and atlas of its , baked by the cut beside the terrain, as globals the terrain, the grass and the details read (FishGroundPaths.hlsl).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePlotManifest.Lot
files.Summary: One laid lot.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePlotManifest
files.Summary: The housing lots a scene cut laid, kept beside the scene's terrain.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePointOfInterest
files.Summary: A generated point of interest in its scene: the transform the site stands at, and the landmark the world map draws for it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePointOfInterestEntrance
files.Summary: A second way into a site the world map draws as its own entry (2026-10-20): another mouth of a cave, the dungeon gate in a large cave's great cavern. Its tier and discovery are the site's.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePointOfInterestSettings
files.Summary: Sits on a generated scene's "Points of Interest" root: which settings its POIs were made with, and the asset they were written to. Its editor offers Regenerate POIs.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePointsOfInterest
files.Summary: The points of interest a generated scene was given, written beside its terrain as <Scene> Points of Interest.asset: the one source of truth everything else is derived from.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropColliders
files.Summary: A scene's baked prop collision: the s its generator wrote, streamed into physics near characters and the camera by . One per scene, at its root; kept by server and client alike.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropCollisionSet.Instance
files.Summary: One collidable prop.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropCollisionSet.Prototype
files.Summary: One kind of collidable prop: its collision mesh (prop space, a simplified stand-in) and its layer.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropCollisionSet
files.Summary: The collidable half of a scene's baked props from one source: a shared collision mesh per prototype and where each collidable prop stands. puts colliders only where they are needed — round every character on the server, round the camera on the client — from pools, so a scene's tens of thousands of trees and rocks never all exist in physics at once.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropSet.Prop
files.Summary: One placed prop.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropSet.Prototype
files.Summary: One kind of prop: the prefab drawn (its LOD group, meshes and materials) and the layer it draws on.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePropSet
files.Summary: A scene's baked props from one source (its scatter's trees and large props, its cliffs' rocks, its rivers' boulders): the prefabs they are made of and where each one stands. The client draws them instanced on the GPU; no prop is a scene object.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneProps
files.Summary: A scene's baked props: the s its generator wrote (scatter, cliffs, boulders), which the client draws instanced. One per scene, on a client-only object at its root.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.ScenePyre
files.Summary: A way light's own open fire (, 2026-10-26, the biome suite's way lights): what its seed says of it and how bright it burns. files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.SceneRoom

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TaggedSceneObjectTargetSelector
files.Summary:
Resolves scene s by Unity tag at runtime. Designed for asset-based Triggers that need to target one or more pre-tagged scene objects — selectors serialized on ScriptableObject assets cannot hold direct scene references, but they can hold a tag string and resolve it at fire time.

The lookup is scoped to the context's scene (whatever scene the event's Target or Initiator lives in). Results are filtered through this selector's .

Tag pre-requisite: the tag must exist in Unity's Tag Manager (ProjectSettings > Tags and Layers). Using an unknown tag logs a warning and yields no targets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TargetSelector
files.Summary:
Abstract base class for selecting targets in an ability or event context. Implementations consume the current (its or serve as the spatial / contextual reference) and yield one or more s for triggers, conditions or actions to operate on.

Asset safety: selectors are serialized inline on Trigger ScriptableObjects via [SerializeReference]. Unity cannot serialize references to scene GameObjects from asset files, so selectors intentionally hold no direct scene references. To "pick a specific scene object" from an asset-based Trigger, use or — they resolve scene objects at runtime by name or tag. For inline (MonoBehaviour-hosted) triggers in a scene, prefer setting at the invocation site so the trigger receives the picked GameObject through standard event flow.

Server-only.
