files.Summary: Hands each terrain tile of a scene what the array terrain shader reads: the tile's index map (its four strongest layers per alphamap texel, baked here from its alphamaps), and the scene's baked texture arrays and layer table.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainArrayLayerParams
files.Summary: The numbers one terrain layer contributes to the array terrain shader, besides its textures.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainArrayLayerSource
files.Summary: One layer of a scene's terrain, in channel order, and every biome slot that painted with it.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainArrayLayerUse
files.Summary: One biome's use of a terrain layer: which biome, and which of its layer slots.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainArrayProvenance
files.Summary: Where each of a scene's terrain layers came from, so its art can be found again — LOCAL overrides included — every time the arrays are baked.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainArraySet
files.Summary: One scene's baked terrain art: the albedo, normal and mask texture arrays the array terrain shader samples, and each layer's tiling and remaps.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainBoundary
files.Summary: MonoBehaviour for defining terrain boundaries. Draws gizmos for visualization and provides boundary size and offset based on terrain data.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.Albedo
files.Summary: A terrain texture set's albedo copy for the grass's colour (GrassAlbedoTexels): every layer's mip pyramid, as the runtime read it back off the GPU. The per-layer header (tiling and tint) is the set's own, written at load.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.Grass
files.Summary: The blade grass's maps of one terrain (GrassTerrain).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.GroundColour
files.Summary: The ground colour map (GroundColourMap) over all of the scene's terrains: per texel the splat-weighted mean colour of the layers as the terrain draws them, and the surface normal; with what it was made from, so the client uses it only when the same terrains stand in the same places drawn with the same texture sets.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.IndexMap
files.Summary: One terrain's index map () as the cut stored it: every alphamap texel's four strongest layers and their weights, two words a texel, row by row — the CPU bake from the alphamaps the cut wrote, the GPU bake's texels bit for bit. A player binds it instead of baking from the alphamaps, so a client build can leave the alphamaps out (ClientTerrainLayerStripper, which checks the map against them first).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.Scatter
files.Summary: The GPU detail scatter's maps of one terrain (DetailScatterTerrain).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake.Tile
files.Summary: One terrain: its heights (shared by both maps' height textures) and its grass and scatter.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBake
files.Summary: A scene's terrain detail maps, baked by the cut (TerrainDetailBaker, client editor): per terrain, what the client's blade grass (GrassTerrain) and GPU detail scatter (DetailScatterTerrain) used to build from the terrain data on every Play — the summed, smoothed and packed density maps, the heights, the water line and holes, the surface layers, the work items' bounds — and the terrain's index map (, what the array terrain draws in a player), plus the grass's colour copies of the terrain texture sets. The client takes a terrain from here in a frame instead of reading it back over ~1,400 frames, and falls back to building it whenever an entry does not match what it would build (, the prototypes and their prefabs, the resolutions, the scatter's density scale) or is marked .

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBiomes.Entry
files.Summary: One detail prototype's biome.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainDetailBiomes
files.Summary: Which biome's spawn rule made each of a terrain's detail prototypes, beside the terrain (written by the scene cut's scatter, TerrainScatter). The scatter makes one prototype per rule and prefab, so the grass on a terrain is several prototypes of one prefab, each painted where its own biome grows it; with this the client knows which biome's look a prototype's blades take (Biomes.BiomeTemplate.GrassTypes), and that its healthy and dry tints are its rule's.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainIndexMap
files.Summary: The terrain's index map: for every texel of a tile's alphamaps, its four strongest layers and their weights, packed into eight bytes. What the array terrain shader reads in place of the alphamaps themselves, so a scene may carry up to layers at the cost of four texel reads a pixel, however many it has.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainIndexMapBaker
files.Summary: Bakes a terrain tile's index map () on the GPU, from the tile's own alphamaps, into an R32G32_UInt render texture the array terrain shader loads.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainLayerTable
files.Summary: A scene's per-layer numbers as one small float texture the array terrain shader loads by layer: column = layer, row = which number. Replaces the per-layer uniform arrays (_FishLayerST[32] and the rest).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainScatterModes

Each is two words (Biomes.BiomeScatterModeWord).

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainSnowHoleFade

One byte a vertex in an R8 map the array terrain shader loads at the vertex (FishTerrainSnowHoles.hlsl), handed to each tile by .

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainTileLayerMap
files.Summary: The arithmetic of per-tile terrain layers (): which of a tile's alphamap channels it keeps, the compacted alphamaps, and how a tile's channel numbers become the scene's layer ids wherever the ground is read by layer (the index map bake, the ground colour, the grass's surface layers). files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TerrainTileLayers
files.Summary: Which of the scene's terrain layers a tile's alphamap channels hold, when the tile carries only the layers it paints (): channel c is scene layer [c], the slice of the scene's texture arrays and the id its index map names.

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.TwoFactorSetupBroadcast
files.Summary:
Broadcast sent by the server after account creation containing encrypted TOTP setup data (otpauth URI and recovery codes) for two-factor authentication.

WARNING: The nonce-derivation scheme on both client and server depends on C# struct field declaration order matching FishNet serialization order. The server sends OtpauthUri first, then RecoveryCodes, and the client consumes them in that exact sequence via receiveNonceCtx.NextNonce(). If these fields are reordered, the nonce streams desynchronize and TOTP silently breaks. DO NOT reorder and .

files.Title: FishMMO.Shared.WorldSceneQueuePositionBroadcast
files.Summary:
Broadcast sent by the WorldServer to a client waiting to be routed to a SceneServer, with its current position in the scene-routing queue. Sent periodically at a server-configured rate.

Position semantics (identical to ):

  • > 0 — Waiting in queue. Display the position to the user.
  • 0 — Routed. A follows; dismiss the wait UI.
  • -1 — Cancelled. The wait was abandoned and the connection is being closed.

Why this exists. The World → Scene hop is the one leg of the connection pipeline that could stall indefinitely with nothing on screen but a loading overlay. A client with no scene instance to go to is held in the WorldServer's queue and re-evaluated every cycle, so the wait is legitimate — but it was completely silent, which is indistinguishable from a hang. This is the login queue's feedback channel applied to the same problem one hop later.

Server-authoritative update rate: The WorldServer controls how often this broadcast is sent. Clients are passive receivers only — there is no request path.

Inline ECA trigger data for world-scene events (scene load, day start, night start, …).

Unlike the asset-based , this type is [Serializable] and lives directly on a host MonoBehaviour so designers can author scene-specific responses inline. Execution semantics — selector fan-out, condition branching, action dispatch — are delegated to so this type stays in lock-step with any future behaviour changes.

files.Summary: Ed25519 signing of JSON manifests, in the exact canonical form the FishMMO client verifies. Deliberately free of ASP.NET, DI and logging dependencies so the shipping server, the operator's offline signing tool and the round-trip test harness all compile the same source file rather than three transcriptions of the same rules.

files.Title: FishMMO.WebShared.ClientGate
files.Summary:
Verifies the X-FishMMO-Client signature on incoming requests. See FishMMO-Unity/Assets/FishMMO/Client/Launcher/ClientApiSigner.cs for the matching client-side producer and the canonical-string format.

The gate is intentionally lightweight: it filters out generic crawlers and casual scanners that don't ship the signed header, and it adds an anti-replay window so a captured header is useful only for 30 seconds. It is NOT an authentication mechanism — the shared secret is compiled into the public client and any motivated attacker can extract it. All real authority comes from the SRP/token flow inside the application.
